target.title: fix(logging): redact Telegram bot tokens from timeout URLs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a fetch to the Telegram Bot API times out, the diagnostic log URL produced by `sanitizeTimeoutLogUrl` still exposes the bot token in the path segment (`/bot<TOKEN>/...`). While the function strips userinfo, query, and hash, it did not redact credential-bearing path segments. Downstream `redactSensitiveText` can be configured off and its token mask (`bot123…cdef`) still leaks part of the token.

Fixes #96982

## Why This Change Was Made

Added a purpose-built `redactBotTokenPath` function in `packages/net-policy/src/redact-sensitive-url.ts` that uses a strict regex (`TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN_PATH_RE`) requiring 6+ digit bot ID + colon or `%3A` + 20+ character secret, keyed by hostname via a redactor registry. This avoids false matches on innocuous `/bot/settings`-style application routes. The redactor is called from both the URL-parsed and fallback-string paths of `sanitizeTimeoutLogUrl`.

## User Impact

All users running Telegram plugin will no longer have their bot tokens logged in plaintext when fetch timeouts occur. The token is replaced with `/bot***` in timeout log messages. Non-Telegram bot paths are unaffected.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test packages/net-policy/src/redact-sensitive-url.test.ts src/utils/fetch-timeout.test.ts` — 46/46 passed (29 net-policy + 17 fetch-timeout)
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check ...` — All matched files use the correct format
- Autoreview: clean (review completed with no actionable findings)

Behavior addressed: Telegram bot tokens in timeout log URLs are now redacted to `/bot***`.
Real environment tested: Unit tests cover hostname matching, percent-encoded colons, fallback string paths, non-matching hostnames, short token IDs/secrets, and edge cases.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `pnpm test packages/net-policy/src/redact-sensitive-url.test.ts src/utils/fetch-timeout.test.ts`
Evidence after fix: 46/46 tests pass, all format checks pass, lint clean.
Observed result after fix: Bot tokens in /bot<TOKEN>/... paths are replaced with /bot*** in `sanitizeTimeoutLogUrl` output.
What was not tested: No live Telegram environment was tested; the fix is purely a log-redaction change with no behavioral impact on actual Telegram API communication.
